title: Why JavaScript Exists

content.explanation: Early websites were static documents that displayed information but could not react to users. Every interaction required communication with a server, creating delays and poor user experiences. Netscape recognized the need for browser-side logic that could provide immediate feedback. This demand for interactivity ultimately led to the creation of JavaScript.
content.example: Form validation moved from servers to browsers for faster feedback.
content.analogy: Instead of calling a teacher for every answer, you solve simple problems yourself.
content.keyTakeaway: JavaScript was created to make websites interactive.

revisionSummary: Static websites created the need for JavaScript.
